title: Brightness results table
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Working scientifically, revision through enquiry (Revolution)
source: Written for science/y6 lesson 32 (Brightness results table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 32: Brightness and voltage: a fair test. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Safety guide: brightness test
points: Use only the torch battery and bulb kit, never mains
Never open plugs, sockets or chargers
An adult is with you; stop if a wire gets warm
Never cut, heat or bite batteries

keywords.def: how hard the cells push the electricity
how much light a bulb gives
say what is the same and different

questions.q: A buzzer with 1 cell is quiet. What happens with 2 cells (within the kit's rating)?
What is the unit of voltage?
Why are three bulbs in a line dimmer than one?
Core: In the simulator or with the kit, test 1 and 2 cells with one bulb, then 1 cell with 1, 2 and 3 bulbs. Record brightness in a table.
questions.a: More cells: brighter; more bulbs in series: dimmer

questions.q: Extend: Write a conclusion for each test using 'the more ... the ...'.
questions.a: 'The more cells, the brighter the bulb.' 'The more bulbs, the dimmer each bulb.'

questions.q: Stretch: Why could too many cells break a bulb?
questions.a: Too much voltage: too much current heats the filament until it breaks

questions.q: Two bulbs in series with one cell are...
questions.a: B) Dimmer than one bulb. They share the same push, so each is dimmer.

questions.q: Big question: why does a 2-battery toy work badly on 1?
